--- title: "Profiles" --- Households and residents of Richmond city, Henrico, and Chesterfield by income relative to area median income (AMI), and a profile of each income band for owners and renters. Everything here comes from the 2020-2024 ACS Public Use Microdata Sample (PUMS) — household-level survey records rather than the published tables the other pages use. ::: callout-warning ## This page covers the core three localities only PUMS reports geography only as Public Use Microdata Areas (PUMAs). The seven PUMAs used here tile Richmond city (2), Henrico (2), and Chesterfield (3) exactly, so every figure is for those three localities and nothing else. The other fourteen localities of the 17-locality region are not included, so totals on this page (381,842 households, 924,266 residents) will not match pages that cover the full region. PUMS households are within 1% of the ACS published counts by tenure for these three localities. ::: ::: callout-note ## How the income bands are defined A household's band compares its income with the HUD FY2026 income limit for its size. The Richmond area's median family income is $113,500; the 4-person limits are 30%, 50%, 80%, 100%, and 120% of that (@tbl-limits). PUMS incomes are inflated to 2026 dollars before the comparison, and the same Richmond-area limits are applied to all seven PUMAs. The **30% AMI or less** band includes 4,823 households (1.3%) with zero or negative income. Vacant units and group quarters are excluded. ::: ::: {#tbl-limits .cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

````` ::: ::: ## Renters sit in the lower income bands, owners in the highest ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-dist-1.png){#fig-dist fig-align='left' fig-alt='Stacked horizontal bar chart of the share of households in each of five AMI bands, for owner households, renter households, and all households in Richmond city, Henrico, and Chesterfield. About 51 percent of owners earn above 120 percent of AMI, against about 20 percent of renters. Renters are spread fairly evenly across the bands, with about 22 percent at 30 percent of AMI or less and 60 percent at 80 percent of AMI or less.' width=100%} ::: ::: - Across the core three, 40.2% of the 381,842 households earn 80% of AMI or less: 28.7% of owners and 60.3% of renters. - 51.3% of owner households earn more than 120% of AMI, against 20.0% of renters. - Renters are spread across the bands rather than concentrated in one: 21.9% are at 30% of AMI or less and 22.6% are in the 51-80% band. - Residents follow the same pattern: 34.8% of the 924,266 people in households live in a household at 80% of AMI or less. ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-counts-1.png){#fig-counts fig-align='left' fig-alt='Stacked column chart of household counts in each of five AMI bands, split into owner and renter households. The above-120-percent band is by far the largest, at about 152 thousand households, mostly owners. The lower four bands each hold between about 41 and 76 thousand households, with renters making up a larger share of the lower bands than of the top one.' width=100%} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-counts .cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Households by AMI band and tenure, and residents by band, 2020-2024. Cells with a coefficient of variation above 30 are suppressed (—); * marks a medium-reliability estimate (CV 15-30). Source: ACS PUMS, HUD FY2026 income limits.
Income band Owners Renters All households Renter share Residents
30% AMI or less 15,381 30,599 45,980 67% 89,386
31-50% AMI 18,685 22,008 40,693 54% 82,973
51-80% AMI 35,453 31,542 66,995 47% 148,878
81-120% AMI 48,626 27,444 76,070 36% 184,680
Above 120% AMI 124,206 27,898 152,104 18% 418,349
All income levels 242,351 139,491 381,842 37% 924,266
````` ::: ::: - Renters outnumber owners only in the 30% AMI or less band, where they are 66.5% of households; the 31-50% AMI band is nearly even (54.1% renters). - Renters make up 18.3% of households above 120% of AMI, against 36.5% of all households. - The largest single group is owner households above 120% of AMI (124,206). Renter households are far more evenly spread, from 22,008 to 31,542 in each band. ## Richmond city has the highest share of lower-income households, but most lower-income renters live in Henrico and Chesterfield ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-geo-1.png){#fig-geo fig-align='left' fig-alt='Grouped bar chart of the share of households at or below 80 percent of AMI, by geography and tenure, for Richmond city, Henrico, Chesterfield, and the three combined, with error bars. Richmond city is highest for owners, renters, and all households, at about 34, 64, and 51 percent. Chesterfield is lowest for owners and for all households, at about 27 and 33 percent.' width=100%} ::: ::: - 50.9% of Richmond city households earn 80% of AMI or less, against 39.1% in Henrico and 33.4% in Chesterfield. - The city's lead holds within each tenure: 64.3% of its renters and 33.9% of its owners are at 80% of AMI or less. - Renters at 80% of AMI or less number 84,149 across the core three, and only 44.6% of them live in Richmond city — the rest are in Henrico and Chesterfield. ## Cost burden falls steeply with income, and low-income renters carry the most ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-burden-1.png){#fig-burden fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel stacked horizontal bar chart of housing cost burden by AMI band, for owners and renters. Among households at 30 percent of AMI or less, about 67 percent of owners and 81 percent of renters pay half or more of income on housing. The share cost-burdened falls with each higher band, to about 2 to 4 percent above 120 percent of AMI.' width=100%} ::: ::: - Among households at 30% of AMI or less, 80.8% of renters and 67.2% of owners pay half or more of income on housing. - Burden falls with each band: renters go from 90.1% cost-burdened (30%+) in the lowest band to 62.0% at 51-80% of AMI and 3.2% above 120%; owners go from 83.2% to 39.4% to 2.4%. - The renter-owner gap is widest at 31-50% of AMI, where 87.0% of renters are cost-burdened against 57.6% of owners (29 points); by 81-120% of AMI the two are within 2 points. - Owner costs include mortgage, taxes, insurance, and utilities; renter costs are gross rent. ## Household makeup shifts from people living alone to couples as income rises ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-hhtype-1.png){#fig-hhtype fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel stacked horizontal bar chart of household type by AMI band, for owners and renters. Living alone is the largest household type among the lowest-income households, at about 58 percent of renters at 30 percent of AMI or less. Couples with and without children make up most households in the higher bands, especially among owners.' width=100%} ::: ::: - Living alone is the most common household type in the lowest band for both tenures: 58.5% of renters and 59.6% of owners. - Single-parent households are 19.4% of renters at 30% of AMI or less, against 4.5% above 120%. - Couples with children are 30.4% of owners above 120% of AMI and 4.9% of owners at 30% or less. ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-earners-1.png){#fig-earners fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel stacked horizontal bar chart of the number of earners per household by AMI band, for owners and renters. The share of households with no earner is highest in the lowest bands, especially among owners, many of whom are retired. Two-earner households dominate the highest bands in both tenures.' width=100%} ::: ::: - No household member earns $5,000 or more in 71.1% of owners and 58.3% of renters at 30% of AMI or less. - At the other end, 63.6% of owners and 63.0% of renters above 120% of AMI have two or more earners. - Most renters at 31-50% of AMI (63.9%) have exactly one earner. - 37.6% of renter households and 35.3% of owner households at 30% of AMI or less include a member with a disability, against 19.4% and 18.9% above 120%. ## Owners in the lowest bands are older; renters are younger at every income level ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-hhage-1.png){#fig-hhage fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel stacked horizontal bar chart of householder age by AMI band, for owners and renters. Among owners, the share aged 65 and over is largest in the lowest band, at more than half, and falls with income. Among renters, householders under 35 are the largest group in the 51 to 80 and 81 to 120 percent bands.' width=100%} ::: ::: - The median householder is 66 for owners at 30% of AMI or less and 52 above 120%; for renters the medians are 45 and 39. - 52.9% of the lowest-income owners are 65 or over — typically a retired homeowner on a fixed income. - Renters aged under 35 are 44.2% of the 51-80% band and 43.9% of the 81-120% band. ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-race-1.png){#fig-race fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel stacked horizontal bar chart of householder race and ethnicity by AMI band, for owners and renters. White non-Hispanic householders are the largest group in every band except the three lowest renter bands, where Black householders are. The White share rises steadily with income among owners and renters alike, and Black householders are a much larger share of the lower bands, particularly among renters.' width=100%} ::: ::: - Black householders are 55.9% of renters at 30% of AMI or less and 23.1% of renters above 120%. - Among owners the same gradient runs from 39.1% at 30% or less to 16.7% above 120%. - White non-Hispanic householders are 69.9% of owners above 120% of AMI. - Hispanic or Latino householders are 12.8% of renters at 31-50% of AMI, their largest share among renter bands. ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-structure-1.png){#fig-structure fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel stacked horizontal bar chart of housing structure type by AMI band, for owners and renters. Owners live overwhelmingly in single-family detached homes in every band. Renters in the lowest bands are concentrated in buildings of 10 or more units and in small multifamily buildings, and single-family homes grow as a share of renters\' housing in the higher bands.' width=100%} ::: ::: - Single-family detached homes house 81.6% of owners at 30% of AMI or less and 90.3% of owners above 120%. - Renters at 30% of AMI or less live in buildings of 2 or more units at a rate of 72.6%; above 120% the share is 56.2%. - 43.4% of renters above 120% of AMI live in single-family homes, against 26.5% of renters at 30% or less. ## Residents: children are most common in the lowest-income renter households, older adults in the lowest-income owner households ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-resage-1.png){#fig-resage fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel stacked horizontal bar chart of resident age by AMI band of the household, for people in owner and renter households. Children under 18 are about a third of residents in the lowest-income renter households, well above their roughly 20 percent share in owner households of every band. People aged 65 and over are the largest age group among residents of the lowest-income owner households.' width=100%} ::: ::: - Children under 18 are 32.6% of residents in renter households at 30% of AMI or less and 20.6% in owner households of that band. - People 65 and over are 35.7% of residents in the lowest-income owner households, against 13.9% above 120% of AMI. - 21.3% of residents in renter households at 30% of AMI or less have a disability, against 9.6% above 120%. ::: {.cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](profiles_files/figure-html/fig-edu-emp-1.png){#fig-edu-emp fig-align='left' fig-alt='Two-panel horizontal bar chart of the share of adults 25 and over with a bachelor\'s degree or higher, and the share of people 16 and over who are employed, by AMI band, for people in owner and renter households. Both shares rise with income, with one small exception: owners\' degree attainment is slightly lower at 31 to 50 percent of AMI than at 30 percent or less. Degree attainment is highest above 120 percent of AMI, at about 63 percent of owners\' adults and 55 percent of renters\'.' width=100%} ::: ::: - Among adults 25 and over, 13.5% of residents of the lowest-income renter households hold a bachelor's degree or higher, against 55.3% above 120% of AMI. - 25.7% of people 16 and over in the lowest-income owner households are employed — low because so many householders are 65 or over — against 37.7% in the lowest-income renter households. - Above 120% of AMI, 74.4% of owner-household residents 16 and over are employed. ## Each band by tenure, side by side ::: {#tbl-profile .cell layout-align="left"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Profile of each AMI band by tenure, 2020-2024. Incomes and housing costs in 2026 dollars; housing cost is monthly owner costs or gross rent among households that pay one; median age is the householder's. Burden shares exclude households with zero or negative income. Cells with a coefficient of variation above 30 are suppressed (—); * marks a medium-reliability estimate (CV 15-30). Source: ACS PUMS, HUD FY2026 income limits.

Above 120% AMI 124,206 $191,690 $2,082 52 2%* 0%*
Renter 30% AMI or less 30,599 $12,904 $1,283 45 90% 81%
31-50% AMI 22,008 $35,766 $1,409 42 87% 45%
51-80% AMI 31,542 $57,862 $1,567 37 62%* 7%*
81-120% AMI 27,444 $88,390 $1,712 37 18%* 1%*
Above 120% AMI 27,898 $155,837 $1,952 39 — —
````` ::: ::: - Median household income runs from $12,904 for renters at 30% of AMI or less to $155,837 above 120%; for owners from $15,166 to $191,690. - Median monthly housing cost for renters rises only from $1,283 to $1,952 across the same bands, which is why burden falls so steeply. - Lowest-income owners pay a median of $943 a month, a figure that includes owners with no mortgage. ::: callout-warning ## Reliability of the profile cells Counts and medians in every band are high-reliability. Shares are noisier where a category is small: of the 459 category-by-band-by-tenure shares estimated, 54 are medium-reliability (CV 15-30) and 9 are low-reliability (CV above 30). All of them are small categories — none exceeds 11.4% of a band, and the low-reliability ones are under 3.2% (for example, severely cost-burdened households above 120% of AMI). Tables suppress low-reliability cells (—) and mark medium ones (*); the stacked bars show every estimate, and a very thin segment should not be read as a precise number. Standard errors come from the 80 Census replicate weights. ::: ::: callout-tip ## What this page shows - **Who is lower-income:** 40.2% of households — 60.3% of renters and 28.7% of owners — earn 80% of AMI or less. - **Where:** Richmond city has the highest share (50.9%), but only 44.6% of lower-income renters live there — most are in Henrico and Chesterfield. - **Burden:** 80.8% of renters at 30% of AMI or less pay half or more of income on housing; above 120% of AMI, 3.2% are cost-burdened. - **Makeup:** the lowest bands are mostly people living alone (58.5% of renters), older owners, and Black householders (55.9% of renters); above 120% of AMI, 78.3% of owners and 53.2% of renters are couples. - **Caveat:** this page covers Richmond city, Henrico, and Chesterfield only, not the 17 localities used on the other pages. :::
